Name: Community Mod Chest
Author: Jared
Description: A collection of community-suggested content additions. Includes new apparel, weapons and armor, character-creation traits (including a Founders Kit starter bundle, a cabin kit, two rain cistern kits, and a stockpile of building materials, all unpacked from one portable kit, and a standalone Extra Rain Cistern Kit perk for more cisterns; the mod's other former starter building-kit perks now live in the separate HomesteadPerks mod), pottery and sculpting items, comfort items (a Garden Trellis that helps planted crops grow faster), fishing gear, village content east of the River Clearing (cross by building the River Bridge, or swim the river at a steep cost in stamina and arrive soaked and weary; strong swimmers cross more easily; bears, wolves and the forest's other roaming predators are refused every move onto the village's seven outdoor tiles and into its buildings (one already standing there in an older save is not moved off) and about half of them back from the Foraging Forest, and a Hunting Stand at your camp turns nearly half of them back), a Clay Shoal with a Clay Barrow for digging clay, a Market Stall for selling trade goods, an enterable Village Inn with a Town Achievement Board that tracks thirteen achievements (a fourteenth, a Harsh Wilds quarry hunt, appears when Harsh Wilds is installed), the last of them King of the Forest, earned when every resident trusts you deeply and the village honours you in full, which teaches a Forest Throne and a Forest Crown, and an enterable Village Academy with seven courses (plus a weekly Sit In on a resident's lecture and a bookshelf for reading alone), including a Carpentry course that unlocks an Outfit Wardrobe (three separate 18-slot sections, one per outfit -- hang gear in a section, then Equip or Unequip that whole outfit in one motion instead of swapping pieces by hand), a Wicker Chair, a Training Post (Practice Strikes once a day for Melee Fighting) and a set of hunt trophies and camp furnishings (a rug, painted canvases, a log bench, potpourri, a framed map, an ice sculpture and a cairn to meditate at). The Village supports long-form civic growth through buildable homes, a Village Hall whose Reputation meter starts at a true neutral and rises toward its ceiling only once every tracked building project AND every villager errand is complete (also visible as a Mental attribute in your character menu), and a Boards room with eight notice boards: Village Standing, Village Projects, and one board each for the Inn Keeper, Miller, Weaver, Apothecary, Professor, and Potter. The villager boards now open directly to their notices without redundant read actions and track active errands, hints, teasers, relationship standing, and recent errand history, and each opens with a live line saying where that villager is right now. Includes the village timeline, resident move-ins, a daily Miller/Weaver schedule (home in their own enterable cottage overnight, working the grindstone or the loom in the village by day, restocking their own trade goods as they go, a nightly Inn visit, and one Academy day every week, each with matching Inn/Academy card art), the Inn Keeper friendship and lost-cat storyline, the Professor's errands and milestone gifts, the Herbalism-gated Apothecary's Cabin with her own nightly Inn visit and weekly Academy day (also with matching card art), and Shadow the Cat as a separate tameable companion. The Inn Keeper and Professor react, once each, to village construction milestones (new cottages, the Village Hall, Village Reputation thresholds) and, for the Professor, to each Academy course you pass. The Inn Keeper also remarks once on each Town Achievement Board achievement you earn (explaining the two the board will not) and, on an evening when two or more residents are at the Inn with you, passes on one line of overheard talk. A communal Town Wood Pile stands in the village square: stock it with twigs, sticks, wood or firewood to keep the six village hearths burning, or let it run dry and watch those fires go out, stocking also builds a separate Player's Pay balance you can withdraw any time as copper nuggets or salt, a reward for the fuel you contributed that never touches what the hearths need. Every winter, snow drifts block all three roads out of the Village until dug clear with a shovel. Four Town Watch guards -- Captain Reeve Sterling, Nella Thorne, Old Corrin and the night-shift Iris Vane -- take up posts around the village with three distinct jobs. Thorne and Corrin walk the Town Square by day and attack any thief or attacker they catch on village ground; Iris Vane keeps the night watch but, once your crimes brand you an enemy of the village, hunts you down anywhere on the map, day or night, and calls the rest of the Watch in rather than fighting you herself -- unlike the other three, village borders do not stop her. Talk to Captain Sterling and he gives you one formal warning the first time your standing turns Suspected -- and once you're Wanted, any guard who spots you reacts without a fight, watching you more closely, which makes a night-time chest search riskier until that suspicion fades again while your Village Crime stays under Wanted (a Cloth Mask or Cloth Hood halves how fast it rises, and Salt or a metal nugget slipped to Sterling, Thorne or Corrin eases that guard's suspicion; Iris Vane takes no bribes), while a conversation with the Captain turns visibly colder. Any of them can be attacked, at a steep and immediate Village Crime cost; guards usually break and flee rather than die, but killing one brands you Banished for good. The Watch is no pushover: all four carry real Blood and armor well beyond a starting-gear brawler's reach, and Captain Sterling hits hardest of all -- winning against a fresh, unequipped character is not the expected outcome. A landed hit leaves a real mark: it raises Bruising alongside Fear and drops an actual wound item -- a Bruise, Abrasion, Laceration, or Puncture depending on severity -- into your inventory that needs Cleaning (or, for the worse ones, Stitching) to stop hurting. Only one guard fights you at a time, so a cornered criminal takes them on back to back, and a guard you nearly beat stays wounded into the next fight; killing one outright (rather than just breaking their morale) is a steep and separate hit to your Village Crime on top of the cost of starting the fight. Best all four and the charges do not drop on their own -- the Inn Keeper hears what happened before you tell her, and only a private conversation owning up to it actually clears your name. A guard you merely rout is out of the Watch for a season before returning to their own post; a guard you kill outright is gone for just a week, and comes back standing in the Village Jail rather than at their old post. Losing to Thorne or Corrin gets you held, not jailed on the spot -- they pin you down and send for the Captain, and Sterling would rather talk you down than fight: he offers to take you in peacefully and lets you walk away up to three times before he stops asking and simply takes you in unhurt, with no Bruising. Attack him yourself instead, or let the whole Watch converge on you at once, and he does not hold back -- he fights for real, harder than any of the other three. Either way, the Watch has you: you wake up in the Village Jail beside the Village Hall, serving a sentence set by what you did -- at least 3 days for any arrest, 7 days for every guard you killed since your last full sentence (capped at 8), or roughly a day for every 8 points of crime if you never spilled blood -- with no way out of the cell until the sentence is served -- a meager daily ration of gruel and water keeps you alive without letting you thrive, backed by an emergency top-up if you ever get dangerously hungry, thirsty, or underweight, and Meditate, Sleep, and a stone-counting distraction help pass the time. A prisoner can pay the warden on the step Salt for one day off the sentence, once per sentence, without clearing any crime, or break rocks in the yard (four hours and a lot of Stamina, twice a day at most) for a quarter of a day off and a matching drop in crime. Captain Sterling also sets community service for anyone with a record: carry wood to the Town Wood Pile or, in winter, dig a snow drift clear, and each finished job takes 6 off your Village Crime; three jobs and a clean record make you his Deputy. A robbed Market Stall can be reported to any guard through Talk, and a few days later the Watch either returns the stolen item to the Village or tells you it found nothing. Guards take turns standing warden on the jail step, in four non-overlapping shifts that cover the whole day between them, and every so often the whole Watch is off the step at once -- and during that rare gap, the cell's own bed can be shoved aside to dig at a hidden tunnel underneath. Get caught digging with the tunnel still exposed and the sentence grows and the tunnel caves back in; finish digging and crawling through clears the remaining sentence, gets you out past the walls, and marks you as an escaped convict -- worse to be caught again. All five named villagers keep a Copper Chest in their own interior -- the Miller's and Weaver's cottages, the Apothecary's Cabin, the Inn, and the Academy. Each adds salt and a little of their own trade stock to it weekly, up to a per-NPC ceiling: the Inn Keeper is the richest buyer in the village, the Miller and Weaver sit mid-tier, and the Apothecary and Professor keep thinner purses but rarer goods. You can sell valuable items to any of them, paid out of that chest's actual contents (so each can only afford what they have actually saved), or rob a chest instead if you are willing to risk being caught by its owner or the night watch. These are personal savings -- the Inn's till and the Academy's tuition account are separate and unaffected. Once the Weaver's regular errands are all done, she has one last thing to teach you: a Climbing Rope pattern, sturdy enough to anchor on the cliff face north of Sett Warren. Fix one there and the path down to Greenfalls opens both ways -- previously impassable in either direction. A Clay Ocarina lets any player craft their own way to tame Shadow the Cat. The Academy Medicine course now grants a craftable payoff (Herb Poultice, Herb Tincture, Spring Tonic), and Old Growth Bark tans hides into leather. New flavor craftables round out the mod: a Toys & Games line (Bone Dice, Spinning Top, Wheeled Horse), Pigment-dyed apparel variants (a garment at a time, or by the armful in a Dye Vat, with a dye run for the Weaver), Stone, Twig and Bone Stockpiles that keep up to 50 loose Stones, Twigs or Bones as one card with a count, charcoal, ochre or billberry Wall Paintings for caves, mud huts and cabins, Curtains for a built window that can be drawn to keep its warmth in or opened to give back its cabin-fever relief, a Scented Candle, a Cat Bed that slowly mends a nearby tamed cat's Care while it is set down, with a treat interaction for all three cats (their descriptions show Care-tier flavor text as it rises and falls, and a cat whose Care stays high turns Content: a calmer camp and, now and then, a small gift), a Cat Bowl that a hungry tamed cat eats meat or fish from on its own at a small cost to its Care, night hunts from which Shadow comes back with a find, and two new starting traits (Potter's Apprentice, Caravan Peddler). A new Quiet Village trait trades away roaming village content for reduced simulation overhead: the Miller, Weaver, Apothecary, Professor, and Potter stay home, at the Academy, or at the Inn instead of commuting or foraging, and none of the four Town Watch guards take up their posts at all. The Copper Chests now tie into Trust and Village Crime: selling into any of the five chests raises that resident's Trust, dragging Salt or a Metal Nugget onto the Miller's chest pays down crime as restitution, a Burglar's Kit shaves a little off a chest search's detection odds (as does the raised Luck of a Born Mark character, which also trims stall robbery and nudges Iron Fishing Rod catches), and the Town board now shows a soft, tiered read of your standing with the village. The residents keep their own count too: chatting, trading and (for the Miller, Weaver and Apothecary) a daily gift, a rare herb for the Apothecary, raise a resident's Trust, and Trust lowers their prices (as do a high Socials skill and a fine face, so the Natural Trader and Leper traits show at all six Trade windows); the Apothecary's board shows her friendship; while you are Wanted every resident charges more and pays less, and once you are Banished they keep you at the worst of those prices; the six residents also greet you coldly while you are Wanted (more briefly once you are Banished) and warm again once your crime falls below 25, with every Trade still working; at Trust 80 with your crime below 25 the Miller, Weaver and Apothecary each give you a keepsake once, in their next Talk (five Wheat Flour, an Ash-Grey Cloth Scarf, a Powerful Healing Potion); the Inn's meals and beds and the Academy's tuition cost more while you are Wanted and more again once you are Banished (the Academy never turns a Banished student away), and the Market Stall earns half as much while you are Banished, its Reputation bonus now growing step by step to +25% at full Reputation instead of appearing only at the top; evenings at the Inn offer Join the Table or Play for the Room when two or more residents are there; with even one resident there you can wager 25 from your Inn Account on a roll of Bone Dice or craftable Loaded Dice (the honest dice favour the house; the loaded pair wins more often but may be caught, which costs the stake and adds to your Village Crime), play Nine Men's Morris on a craftable Morris Board (better Focus, better odds) or arm-wrestle a resident for the same stake (better Fitness, better odds, 8 Stamina a bout); the Inn Counter also posts one small odd job each morning (a Stone, Rope, Ash or a Clay Bowl for a copper nugget; see the odd-jobs board in the README); passing an Academy course hands you a framed diploma for it (a little Comfort for camp, one per course); crossing paths with the Apothecary or the Professor on the road earns a word, a little Trust and a lift in Morale; commissions let you pay the Miller, the Weaver or the Inn Keeper (a Salt, a nugget or a coin dragged onto them) for ten Wheat Flour, a Large Cloth or a hunter's Doe Carcass, waiting in their room a day or two later; and a Fugitive arrives already known to the Watch. With Advanced Copper Tools installed, the Inn Keeper's pantry also stocks its Focus, Calming and Warming Teas, and with Herbs & Fungi installed, three of its baked foods. With Sirus23 Mod Collection installed, the pantry also adds its Sheep Cheese, the Weaver stocks its Wool Yarn and Felted Wool and offers a one-time wool yarn errand, and the Quilted Cap and Quilted Vest can be padded with its raw Wool into warmer Wool-Quilted versions. The three non-Sterling Town Watch guards (Thorne, Corrin, Vane) now have a friendly Talk option of their own, the Market Stall can toggle a cosmetic awning, village interiors work like a cabin room (Insulation, Cabin Fever, 200 Comfort; buildable Windows, and a buildable Fireplace in the Jail Cell), an autumn deadfall now blocks the Pine Trail route in season alongside the winter snow drifts, and a spring thaw floods the Clay Shoal ford -- wait the water down on the bank, or build the new Plank Causeway at Clay Shoal and lay it across to open the road at once, and every summer a bramble thicket chokes the Stillwater Meadow to Sett Warren trail until you cut it back with a sickle or tear through it by hand. The first time Village Reputation reaches its full mark, a Founder's Monument appears once in the Village and adds 6 Comfort while you are there. The village keeps the seasons too, once you are introduced: in autumn the Inn Keeper asks for dried food to stock the Inn's pantry (a small reward), on the first day of summer the six residents ease their prices a little for a day (about 1.3% off a stranger's price, nearer 2% from a resident who already trusts you, and never enough to beat the Wanted markup), and when winter closes the roads the residents gather at the Inn for a snowed-in supper you can join once that winter (Morale +35). A sixth resident, the Potter, takes a room at the Inn once you are introduced: he sells painted pottery and raw Clay, works the market corner of the Village on the summer market day, asks you once to fire him a plain clay bowl, plate, jar or vase in your own kiln (3 Salt and a little Trust), and has his own board in the Village Hall. Wearing three or more pieces of the mod's cold-weather apparel at once (scarves, coats, hoods, wraps, long johns and the quilted pieces) adds a little perceived warmth on top of what each piece gives. With the optional DurosCoinage installed, the Inn Keeper's chest also holds a Duros coin and the Market Stall can pay its takings in coins (Collect as Coins); with Herbs & Fungi installed, the Professor's Herbalism stock can include Hemp Seeds. By day the Village Path carries the distant sounds of the settlement: a rooster, a hen, a cow and a goat.
